exposure: Polyhydramnios detection by gestational age-specific centile method (amniotic fluid volume >95th centile)
Polyhydramnios detection by Amniotic Fluid Index >24 cm
outcome: Composite adverse perinatal outcome (Major fetal structural malformations, stillbirths, 5 min Apgar score <7 at 5 min, NICU admission >24 hours, Jaundice requiring phototherapy, early neonatal death)
cohort: The study included 936 singleton pregnancies with polyhydramnios and a gestational age of >28 weeks.
finding: The Amniotic Fluid Index method (>24cm) showed a significantly increased incidence of adverse perinatal outcomes compared to the gestational age-specific centile method and is considered a better choice for labeling polyhydramnios.
mod_finding: The study revealed a statistically significant increased incidence of cesarean rates in the AFI>24cm group when compared with the gestational age-specific centile group.
followup_time: Until the early neonatal period (including NICU admission >24 hours and early neonatal death)
